```{r Single-PFAS-Volcano-Knitted}
      collapse = "\n"),
    face = "bold", family = "Times", size = 12))

# Printing out the plots
print(individ_mwas)
```

<h3 style="text-align: center"> 5.3. Sensitivity Analysis Volcano Plot (5-PFAS mixture) </h3>

As a sensitivity analysis, I generated a volcano plot for a 5-PFAS mixture that included MeFOSAA (PFOS, PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS, and MeFOSAA). This figure mirrors the primary MWAS volcano plot and is used to assess whether adding MeFOSAA changes the overall pattern of effect sizes and statistically prioritized metabolomic features.
```{r 5-PFAS-Volcano}
# Calculating the number of significant values for the 4-PFAS mixture
n_sig_5 = nrow(qg_comp_5_SIG)
# Calculating the total number of values in the 4-PFAS analysis
n_total_5 = nrow(qg_comp_5_FULL)

# Converts an FDR=0.20–scaled p-value cutoff (0.2 × proportion significant) into the volcano plot y-value (-log10 p) for the horizontal “significance” line.
threshold <- -log10(n_sig_5 /n_total_5 * 0.2) #(significant/total N)*p-value

# Creating the volcano plot for the 4-PFAS mixture
mefosaa_mwas <- ggplot() +
  # Adding grey points below the line
  geom_point(
    data = subset(qg_comp_5_FULL, -log10(p.value) <= threshold), 
    aes(x = psi, y = -log10(p.value)), 
    color = "darkgray") +
  # Adding red points above the line to signify statistical significance
  geom_point(
    data = subset(qg_comp_5_FULL, -log10(p.value) > threshold), 
    aes(x = psi, y = -log10(p.value)), 
    color = "red") +
  # Adding a horizontal line to denote significance threshold
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = threshold, 
    color = "red", 
    linetype = "dashed") +
  # Adding labels and titles
  # Adding labels and titles
  labs(title = paste(strwrap("Figure 5. Sensitivity analysis of the association between metabolic features and a mixture of 5 PFAS (4 PFAS mixture + MeFOSAA) in the HOME Study (2003 to 2006, N = 264)", width = 70), collapse = "\n"), 
       x = "Log2-Fold Change in Ion Intensity",
       y = "-Log10 (p-value)") +
  # Applying the black and white theme
  theme_bw() +
  # Modifying theme to remove x-axis grid lines and set font and axis color
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
    text = element_text(family = "Times"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black"),
    plot.title = element_text(face   = "bold", size   = 13, family = "Times", hjust  = 0.4))

# Print the plot
print(mefosaa_mwas)
```

<h2 style="text-align: center"> **6. Pathway Enrichment Analysis-Figures** </h2>

In the next section, I provide the code used to generate the bubble plots. This code was adapted from **Elvira Fleury** and extended to incorporate KEGG BRITE pathways and to overlay individual PFAS results alongside the 4-PFAS mixture.

Bubble plots were used to summarize pathway-level results because they simultaneously convey statistical significance and enrichment strength across many pathways. In these figures, the x-axis reflects statistical evidence, point size represents enrichment magnitude, and color distinguishes exposure models, allowing efficient comparison of pathway patterns across mixtures and individual PFAS.

<h3 style="text-align: center"> 6.1. Bubble plot (4-PFAS mixture & single PFAS) </h3>
This bubble plot summarizes metabolic pathways enriched in association with the 4-PFAS mixture (PFOS, PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS) based on mummichog pathway enrichment analysis. Each point represents a metabolic pathway, with horizontal position reflecting statistical evidence and point size indicating enrichment strength.

Pathways were ordered by statistical significance for the 4-PFAS mixture and grouped according to superpathways defined in the KEGG BRITE database [(KEGG BRITE Database)](https://www.genome.jp/kegg/brite.html). Superpathway brackets were added manually as a presentation layer to improve readability; all pathway ordering and enrichment statistics are unchanged.

Overall, the plot highlights pathways most consistently implicated by the PFAS mixture, providing a pathway-level summary that complements feature-level MWAS results and helps prioritize biological processes for downstream interpretation.
```{r Individual_BubblePlot_4_PFAS, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Creating a helper function to preserve a consistent factor order.
add_levels <- function(x, levels) {
  levels <- unique(c(levels, x))
  factor(x, levels = levels)
}

# Importing the data I need for the 4-PFAS Mixture mixture and locking in the order for pathways
mummi_for_plot <- mummi_for_plot<-read.csv("/Users/amber/Desktop/Metabolomics/Analyses/Data/2023.06.04.mummi_4pfas_res.csv") 
mummi_for_plot$X1 <- add_levels(mummi_for_plot$X1, mummi_for_plot$Pathway)

# Creating a new 'skeleton copy' of the 4-PFAS dataset
blank <- mummi_for_plot
blank[, -(1:3)] <- NA


# Importing the full individual-PFAS mummichog results, then aligning them to the mixture pathway set so all plots share the same pathway universe and y-axis ordering (Pathway -> X1 mapping).
mummi_for_plot_ind <- read.csv("/Users/amber/Desktop/Metabolomics/Analyses/Data/individual.csv")

# Keeping only the pathways that also appear in the mixture results (so comparisons are apples-to-apples)
mummi_for_plot_ind <- subset(mummi_for_plot_ind, Pathway %in% mummi_for_plot$Pathway)

# Droping the existing X1 (we re-attach X1 from the mixture results to enforce consistent factor ordering)
mummi_for_plot_ind <- subset(mummi_for_plot_ind, select = -X1)

# Merging in the mixture-derived X1 index so individual PFAS results inherit the same y-axis pathway order
mummi_for_plot_ind <- merge(mummi_for_plot_ind, mummi_for_plot[, c("Pathway", "X1")], by = "Pathway")

# Removing rows with missing values (typically introduced by filtering/merging) before plotting
mummi_for_plot_ind <- na.omit(mummi_for_plot_ind)


# Individual PFAS
# Creating a dataset with all NAs except Pathways and removing datasets
pfas_map <- mummi_for_plot[!duplicated(mummi_for_plot$X1), 1:3]
  pfas_map$X1 <- factor(pfas_map$X1)
pfas_map_X1 <- data.frame(X1 = pfas_map[, 1])

# PFOS
pfos_for_plot <- mummi_for_plot_ind %>% filter(PFAS == 'PFOS')
    pfos_for_plot<-pfos_for_plot[!is.na(pfos_for_plot$PFAS),]
    pfos_for_plot <- merge (pfos_for_plot, pfas_map_X1, by="X1", all=TRUE)
# PFNA
pfna_for_plot <- mummi_for_plot_ind %>% filter(PFAS == 'PFNA')
    pfna_for_plot<-pfna_for_plot[!is.na(pfna_for_plot$PFAS),]
    pfna_for_plot <- merge (pfna_for_plot, pfas_map_X1, by="X1", all=TRUE)
# PFHxS
pfhxs_for_plot <- mummi_for_plot_ind %>% filter(PFAS == 'PFHxS')
    pfhxs_for_plot<-pfhxs_for_plot[!is.na(pfhxs_for_plot$PFAS),]
    pfhxs_for_plot <- merge (pfhxs_for_plot, pfas_map_X1, by="X1", all=TRUE)
# PFOA
pfoa_for_plot <- mummi_for_plot_ind %>% filter(PFAS == 'PFOA')
    pfoa_for_plot<-pfoa_for_plot[!is.na(pfoa_for_plot$PFAS),]
    pfoa_for_plot <- merge (pfoa_for_plot, pfas_map_X1, by="X1", all=TRUE)

# Creating a plot
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12, base_family = "Times New Roman"))

# Mixture bubble plot with all the individual chemicals
# Plot using ggplot
four_ind_mummi <- ggplot() +
geom_point(data = pfoa_for_plot, aes(x = -log10(Gamma), y = X1, size = Hits.sig / Expected, color = "PFOA")) + # PFOA LAYER
  geom_point(data = pfna_for_plot, aes(x = -log10(Gamma), y = X1, size = Hits.sig / Expected, color = "PFNA")) + # PFNA LAYER
  geom_point(data = pfhxs_for_plot, aes(x = -log10(Gamma), y = X1, size = Hits.sig / Expected, color = "PFHxS")) + # PFHxS LAYER
  geom_point(data = pfos_for_plot, aes(x = -log10(Gamma), y = X1, size = Hits.sig / Expected, color = "PFOS")) + # PFOS LAYER
  geom_point (data=mummi_for_plot, aes(x = -log10(Gamma), y = X1, size = Hits.sig / Expected, color = "4-PFAS Mixture")) + #4-PFAS mixture level
  scale_size_continuous(guide = guide_legend(title = "Enrichment Factor")) +
  labs(x = "-Log10 (p-value)", 
       y = "", 
       color = "Type of PFAS") + # plot labels
  scale_color_manual(values = c("4-PFAS Mixture" = "black", 
                                "PFOA" = "#3C8DC4", "PFNA" = "#FF9A3F", 
                                "PFHxS" = "#942E2E", "PFOS" = "hotpink"), # manually set colors
                     breaks = c("4-PFAS Mixture", "PFOA", "PFNA", "PFHxS", "PFOS")) + # manually set order of PFAS to be consistent 
  scale_y_discrete(labels = mummi_for_plot$Pathway) + # Set x-axis labels to unique "Pathway" values
    scale_x_continuous(expand =  c(0, 0), limits = c(1, 2.6), breaks = seq(1, 2.5, 0.5)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", 
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5), 
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14), 
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), 
        legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.box = "vertical")
```

After this, the figure will look like this:
```{r Individual_BubblePlot_4_PFAS_Render, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=15, dpi=200, out.widtheval=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
print(four_ind_mummi)
```

An important note, for plots with many or long pathway labels, adjusting figure dimensions (particularly height) may be necessary for readability. This can be done either by specifying dimensions in Quarto or when exporting the plot (e.g., with ggsave()). 

After generating the base bubble plot, I added the KEGG BRITE Superpathway brackets manually as a post-processing annotation. This was my final result:
```{r Individual_BubblePlot_Final, echo=FALSE, fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("Figures/4-PFAS Mixture Bubbleplot.png")
```

<h3 style="text-align: center"> 6.2. Sensitivity Analysis bubble plot </h3>
As a sensitivity analysis, this bubble plot summarizes pathway enrichment results for a 5-PFAS mixture that includes MeFOSAA. Using the same analytic steps as the primary mixture and individual-PFAS pathway analyses, the figure compares these results with those from the 4-PFAS mixture to evaluate whether the biological pathways implicated by prenatal PFAS exposure remain consistent when MeFOSAA is included, providing a pathway-level assessment of robustness to mixture specification.
```{r 5PFAS_BubblePlot, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=15, dpi=200}
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12, base_family = "Times New Roman"))

# Loading in the mixture data
# 5-PFAS Mixture
mummi_for_plot_5 <- read.csv("/Users/amber/Desktop/Metabolomics/Analyses/Data/2023.07.19.mummi_5PFAS with 4-PFAS pathways too.csv") 
# 4-PFAS Mixture
mummi_for_plot_4 <- read.csv("/Users/amber/Desktop/Metabolomics/Analyses/Data/2023.07.19.mummi_4PFAS with 5-PFAS pathways too.csv") 

# 5-PFAS Mixture bubble plot 

# Converting X1 to an ordered factor (in its current row order) so ggplot preserves the intended pathway ordering on the y-axis for both the 4-PFAS and 5-PFAS datasets.
mummi_for_plot_5$X1 <- factor(mummi_for_plot_5$X1, levels = unique(mummi_for_plot_5$X1))
mummi_for_plot_4$X1 <- factor(mummi_for_plot_4$X1, levels = unique(mummi_for_plot_4$X1))

# Plotting using ggplot
mummi5 <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = mummi_for_plot_4, aes(x = -log10(Gamma), y = X1, size = Hits.sig / Expected, color="4PFAS")) + #4PFAS layer 
geom_point(data = mummi_for_plot_5, aes(x = -log10(Gamma), y = X1, size = Hits.sig / Expected, color="5PFAS")) + #5PFAS layer 
  scale_size_continuous(guide = guide_legend(title = "Enrichment Factor")) +
  labs(x = "-Log10 (p-value)", y = "", color = "Type of PFAS") +
    scale_color_manual(
    values = c("4PFAS" = "black", "5PFAS" = "hotpink"),
    breaks = c("4PFAS", "5PFAS"),
    labels = c("4-PFAS Mixture", "5-PFAS Mixture")) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = mummi_for_plot_5$Pathway) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", 
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5), 
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14), 
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), 
        legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.box = "vertical")
```

```{r 5_BubblePlot_Final, echo=FALSE, fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("Figures/5-PFAS Mixture Bubbleplot.png")
```

<h3 style="text-align: center"> 6.3. Pathway overlap Venn diagram </h3>
To compare pathway signals across individual PFAS, I created a Venn diagram summarizing overlap in significantly enriched pathways (p(Gamma) < 0.05) for PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS, and PFOS. This visualization highlights which pathways are shared across PFAS versus those that appear more compound-specific, providing a quick summary of consistency in pathway enrichment patterns across the individual exposure models.
```{r venn_plot, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=9, dpi=300}
# Creating list of PFAS to include for the Venn diagram 
mummi_list <- list(
  PFOA  = unique(na.omit(pfoa_for_plot$Pathway)),
  PFNA  = unique(na.omit(pfna_for_plot$Pathway)),
  PFHxS = unique(na.omit(pfhxs_for_plot$Pathway)),
  PFOS  = unique(na.omit(pfos_for_plot$Pathway)))

# Creating the Venn Diagram
venn <- ggvenn(
  mummi_list,
  fill_color = c("#3C8DC4", "#FF9A3F", "#942E2E", "hotpink"),
  stroke_size = 0.5,
  set_name_size = 4,
  text_size = 3.5) +
  labs(title = paste(
    strwrap("Figure 8. Venn diagram of metabolic pathways associated with 4 PFAS in the HOME study (2003 to 2006; N=264)", width = 70),
    collapse = '\n'), 
    subtitle = "Pathways with p(Gamma) < 0.05") +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 30, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10),
        plot.title = element_text(family = "Times", size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(family = "Times", size = 16, hjust = 0.5))

print(venn)
```
